optimizations.title: Optimization: In-Place Reversal
task: The previous `reverse_array` implementation utilized an 'out-of-place' approach, allocating a secondary array and resulting in O(n) Space Complexity. This can be optimized to an 'in-place' O(1) Space operation using a two-pointer technique.
1. Remove the initialization of the secondary array (`result = []`).
2. Instantiate two pointer variables: `left` starting at 0, and `right` starting at `len(arr) - 1`.
3. Implement a `while left < right:` loop. Within this block, swap the values located at `arr[left]` and `arr[right]`.
4. Increment the `left` pointer and decrement the `right` pointer to converge towards the center.
5. Observe that the reversal is achieved without requiring additional proportional memory.

optimizations.title: Optimization: Set-Based Deduplication
task: A standard anti-pattern for deduplication involves iterating over an array and evaluating containment against a secondary tracking list (`if item not in unique_list`). This dynamic forces an O(n^2) scaling issue. Optimization requires utilizing Hash-based structures.
1. Remove the secondary tracking list and the linear containment check (`if item not in...`).
2. Replace the iterative logic with native Set architecture. A Set resolves element unicity inherently.
3. Transform the original array using `set(arr)` to perform instantaneous deduplication.
4. Cast the resulting Set back to a list format. Verify the computational complexity shift from O(n^2) to an efficient O(n).
